entry.summary:
Understanding the static Keyword in Java
In Java, static keyword is powerful feature used primarily for memory management. It is one of those small keywords with big implications—allowing us to create members that belong to class rather than instances of class. This post explores how static works with variables, methods, blocks, and nested classes, along with examples. static Keyword?
The static keyword indicates that a particular member belongs to the class itself and not to instances of the class. That means: Static variables and methods are shared among all instances. Static blocks execute once, at the time of class loading. Static members can be accessed without creating object of class.
